newsitem.title: GERMANY: BMW sees H2 earnings up but pound hitting Rover.
newsitem.headline: BMW sees H2 earnings up but pound hitting Rover.

text.p: The head of German carmaker BMW AG said earnings growth in the second half of 1997 should continue at the pace of the first six months but added that the strong pound was hurting earnings at UK unit Rover.
"The chances of continuing the trend of the first half aren't bad," BMW chief executive Bernd Pischetsrieder said in an interview with Handelsblatt published on Monday, referring to the BMW group.

The weakness of the mark, which boosts export income, may have a stronger positive impact on earnings during the period, Pischetsrieder said, but he added that the impact of currency movements on earnings was limited because BMW had hedged itself.
Pischetsrieder also said that currency movements had been adverse in some areas, including at Rover where the strong pound could hamper efforts to return to profit from the year 2000.
"If the British currency remains so strong, it could become more difficult to hit the black at Rover as planned, especially when taking into account that Rover is expected to boost exports," he said.
The BMW chief also confirmed the company was developing a sport utility vehicle, even though the group is already represented in the segment by Land Rover and Range Rover cars.
Pischetsrieder would not comment on when such a vehicle would be introduced and that it might be based on existing BMW estate cars.
